title: We are living in Cloud 3.0
oneliner: Cloud 1.0 hosted workloads, 2.0 ran cloud-native apps - 3.0 is the AI era: AI workloads in the cloud, hybrid-connected to on-premises, scaled effortlessly on provider AI services.
says: We are now in the Cloud 3.0 era. Cloud 2.0 was about deploying and running workloads in public or private cloud. Cloud 3.0 means running AI workloads in the cloud, connecting those AI workloads to on-premises systems through hybrid cloud, using the AI capabilities cloud providers offer, and scaling AI systems effortlessly.
explained: Era labels are useful when they mark a real shift in what the platform is for. In 1.0 the cloud was cheaper hosting. In 2.0 it was the place cloud-native applications were built - containers, microservices, managed everything. In 3.0 the center of gravity moves: the cloud becomes the operating layer for AI - model services, GPU capacity, vector stores, agent runtimes - and the hard problems become integration problems: hybrid connectivity to the systems of record, and scaling inference economically.

The hybrid point is the one enterprises feel most. Their data and core systems are still on-premises or in private cloud; the AI capabilities are in the public cloud. Cloud 3.0 architecture is largely the art of bridging those two worlds safely - which is exactly the problem set his Season 1 infrastructure episodes work through.
takeaway: In Cloud 3.0 the architect's job shifts from 'move workloads to cloud' to 'connect AI services to the systems and data that already exist.'
